# Calculating ∫ -3*x**4*cos(x) dx

## Setting Up Integration by Parts

I'll use repeated integration by parts (tabular method) for ∫ x⁴cos(x) dx, then multiply by -3.

**Tabular Method:**

| Derivatives (of x⁴) | Sign | Integrals (of cos(x)) |
|---|---|---|
| x⁴ | + | sin(x) |
| 4x³ | − | −cos(x) |
| 12x² | + | −sin(x) |
| 24x | − | cos(x) |
| 24 | + | sin(x) |

## Computing ∫ x⁴cos(x) dx

∫ x⁴cos(x) dx = x⁴sin(x) + 4x³cos(x) − 12x²sin(x) − 24x·cos(x) + 24sin(x) + C

## Multiplying by −3

∫ −3x⁴cos(x) dx = −3x⁴sin(x) − 12x³cos(x) + 36x²sin(x) + 72x·cos(x) − 72sin(x) + C

## Verification (by differentiating)

- d/dx[−3x⁴sin(x)] = −12x³sin(x) − 3x⁴cos(x)
- d/dx[−12x³cos(x)] = −36x²cos(x) + 12x³sin(x)
- d/dx[36x²sin(x)] = 72x·sin(x) + 36x²cos(x)
- d/dx[72x·cos(x)] = 72cos(x) − 72x·sin(x)
- d/dx[−72sin(x)] = −72cos(x)

Sum: all terms cancel except **−3x⁴cos(x)** ✓

<answer>-3*x**4*sin(x) - 12*x**3*cos(x) + 36*x**2*sin(x) + 72*x*cos(x) - 72*sin(x) + C</answer>
